note: Server-side verification of a Digest credential: parse the header, recompute the response digest and compare. Upstream has no verify helper, so the node runner composes DIGEST.parseAuthorizationRest with DIGEST.computeHash the way a server would; an algorithm no hash implementation supports is reported as a rejection (false) on both sides rather than an error. Every valid response digest in this file was produced by the upstream oracle.

cases.note: RFC 7616 spells the response in lowercase hex (LHEX)
cases.deviation: VerifyDigest compares the response case-insensitively (still in constant time) because clients disagree about hex case, where upstream compares the exact string. Not a credential bypass: case-folding hex is a 1:1 relabelling of the same digest, so it admits nobody who does not already hold the correct response

args: Digest username="alice", realm="Parity", nonce="deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef", uri="/protected", response="", qop=auth, nc=00000001, cnonce="0a4f113b", algorithm=MD5
cases.note: both sides must fail: an empty response is not a credential
cases.deviation: the port refuses to parse a credential whose response digest is empty; upstream parses it and only reports the rejection at verification time — same rejection, one layer apart
